profile.campus: Data4 Madrid MAD2 (San Agustín del Guadalix)
profile.address: San Agustín del Guadalix, Madrid, Spain
profile.reading:
This facility is part of Data4's Madrid data center campus, one of ten campuses the French-headquartered, pan-European colocation operator runs across France, Italy, Spain, Poland, Germany, and Greece, totaling roughly 165,000 square meters of IT space and 1.5 GW of power capacity company-wide, per Data4's own site. The OpenStreetMap record for this building carried no operator name prior to this update; this registry corrects that gap directly, since the building's own designation, MAD2-DC02, is an exact match to Data4's published Madrid campus building-naming convention.

Data4's Madrid presence spans two distinct sites: MAD1, in Alcobendas at Avenida de la Industria 15, and MAD2, a separate, newer site in San Agustín del Guadalix, a municipality north of Madrid. This building, MAD2-DC02, is the second data hall built on the San Agustín del Guadalix site, alongside MAD2-DC01, on a second, physically separate Madrid-area campus from MAD1.

Data4 markets its data centers on modular, scalable design principles, sustainability commitments including free-cooling systems suited to the Iberian climate, and connectivity to major European internet exchange points; the Madrid market itself has grown substantially as a European data center hub in recent years alongside Data4's French home market. This registry has not located Data4's own building-by-building capacity or square-footage disclosure for MAD2-DC02 specifically, so no it_capacity_mw or technical_space_sqft figure is asserted for this individual building; Data4 discloses these figures at the company and campus level rather than per building in its public materials found this session. Data4 was founded in 2006 and is described in the company own 2019-era published materials as controlled by AXA, the French insurance and asset-management group. Madrid overall has grown into one of Europe leading data center hubs over the past decade, driven by favorable connectivity, renewable energy availability, and government incentives for digital infrastructure investment in Spain.
